title: Ground station events
description:
One object per message on gsu/{station_id}/events, carrying a batch of things that happened.

**This is the one channel that is a ledger rather than a stream, and every rule elsewhere in this contract inverts here.** Telemetry is current state and may be dropped, because a newer frame replaces it in a second. An event has no newer version: a transmission recorded at 03:12, a proximity alert, a credential renewal that failed, a floodlight that drew no current. Losing it loses the fact.

That is why the station buffers events through an outage and telemetry is discarded, and why this channel is acknowledged when nothing else is. A station keeps every unacknowledged event on local storage - across reboots - and re-sends until the platform says it has them.

Delivery is **at-least-once**, never exactly-once: an acknowledgement can be lost after the platform has stored a batch, in which case the station sends it again. Consumers deduplicate on `id`, which is why `id` is required and must be globally unique.

events.description: Oldest first. Capped so a station reconnecting with a long backlog delivers it in batches rather than in one frame the relay would refuse - see transport.md for the pacing rule. A station with more waits for the acknowledgement of one batch before sending the next.

id.description: Globally unique, generated by the station when the event is recorded and never reused - including across a re-send. **This is the deduplication key**, and it is a UUID rather than a counter because a counter is only unique within one station's storage: a box whose local store is rebuilt starts counting again, and a platform deduplicating on that would silently discard real events from a station it had seen before.

seq.description:
Monotonic within the station's current local store, increasing by one. This is the **acknowledgement cursor**, not the identity - `events.ack` names a seq and the station may then delete everything up to it.

It can go backwards exactly once per store rebuild, which is not an error: the platform acknowledges what it is sent and keeps deduplicating on `id`, so a restarted counter costs nothing. Kept separate from `id` because the two jobs are different, and one field doing both is what makes a rebuilt store lose data.

at.description: When it happened, by the station's own clock, ISO 8601 with an offset. Not when it was sent - the whole point of this channel is that those differ by the length of an outage.

clock.description: Whether `at` is worth trusting. A station with no battery-backed clock that has not reached a time source since boot produces timestamps that are internally consistent and absolutely wrong, and an event log that cannot say so is worse than one with gaps - somebody will read those times as fact. `unsynced` means order is meaningful and absolute time is not. Absent means the station did not say, which a consumer should treat as `unsynced` on any station known to lack an RTC (enrolment.md section 6).

type.description: What happened, as a dotted name: `radio.transmission`, `adsb.alert`, `power.low`, `credential.renewal_failed`, `light.no_draw`, `uplink.restored`. The station owns this vocabulary and may add to it - the platform stores and displays unknown types rather than dropping them, exactly as it ignores unknown telemetry kinds, because an event it does not recognise is still something that happened at a site.

severity.description: The same three words as `health.conditions[].severity`, deliberately. A condition is a state that is currently true; an event is a thing that occurred. The same underlying fault usually produces both, and using one vocabulary means an operator does not have to learn two.

detail.description: One line for a person, not a parser.

data.description: Anything structured the event carries - a frequency, a contact's icao, a recording's local name. Free-form by design and **non-normative**: consumers may display it and must not require any particular key, because the set differs per `type` and the station is the side that learns new ones first.
